Preregistered local experiment · accuracy-driven implementation decision

Decision: adopt the smooth measurement implementation

The selection metric is agreement with an independent QuTiP conditional state. A higher logical memory fidelity alone cannot win this comparison. The smooth implementation must also pass outcome-distribution accuracy, continuous-sampler validation, and the registered long-horizon numerical gates.

The smooth resource and matching continuous sampler are now the default for new reference CLI runs. Historical binned mode remains available for reproduction. Raw observations, engineering tolerances and the pre-run protocol remain available below.

Accuracy and decision ruleEight-cycle resultsRare-event analysisMethod and metric citationsData and limits

The accuracy metric

A = ∫ pQuTiP(y) |⟨ψQuTiP(y) | ψmodel(y)⟩|² dy.

The inner term is squared quantum-state fidelity: 1 means identical pure states up to global phase. We average it over the reference outcome distribution and report the worst accuracy over the fixed held-out inputs. The squared-fidelity convention follows Jozsa (1994). This reference weighting and the numerical acceptance budget are our engineering choices, not thresholds prescribed by that paper.

Before these runs, acceptance was set at A ≥ 99.999%, with outcome total variation ≤10⁻⁴. The new test uses six freshly displaced cardinal states, seed26111923, both extraction axes, two resource widths, and ancillary cutoff refinement from512 to768. It is a finite-data-operator comparison at96 data levels; it does not establish a worst-case channel bound.

The inverse-CDF sampler uses the positive Gaussian-mixture representation of the same smooth wavefunction density. Its quantile residual and independently integrated CDF are checked. The empirical outcome check uses65,536 samples per input/axis/resource combination, with a strict familywise95% DKW–Massart bound. No Monte Carlo intervals are attached to the deterministic fidelity integrals.

Matched eight-cycle experiment

Both implementations use nominal displacement/readout settings(.20,.05,.90), nearest-lattice feedback, Δ=.30,512 trajectories for each of six input states, and the historical seed26111901. The binned observations are frozen controls whose hashes and input noise arrays are checked. Smooth outcomes use a matching continuous sampler. Common random numbers do not force the two models to have identical measurement histories.

Population limits are ensemble mean top-decile mass <.01% and every trajectory <1%, checked at every recorded substep. The final4096-versus5120 paired fidelity interval must fit entirely within±1 percentage point at every cycle. Trajectory intervals are pointwise, stratified over the six states; they exclude model uncertainty. Logical memory fidelity is a physical performance measure for this protocol, while A measures implementation accuracy against QuTiP.

At cutoff5,120, the selected binned trajectory also exceeds the1% boundary limit at an intermediate substep, despite passing its historical cycle-end checks. The continuous run passes at every recorded substep. These indices were selected from the old binned run before the new experiment. Replay errors against full-batch observations are saved in the audit. The plots identify where energy changes, not a universal physical mechanism. Differences across stochastic histories alone cannot prove that every rare high-energy event is artificial.

Decision interpretation and maximum observed energy jumps across all trajectories are recorded in summary.json. This is a combined numerical implementation change: the resource representation and its matching sampler change together. The experiment does not separately assign their contributions. It does not add damping, loss, stabilization or decoder retraining.

Method and metric sources

The physical method is finite-energy GKP syndrome extraction using a fresh ancilla, SUM interaction and homodyne measurement, followed by a displacement correction. The local update My=φ(y−q) is the reduced form of the explicit circuit; momentum extraction uses the Fourier conjugate. See Gottesman, Kitaev & Preskill (2001) and Grimsmo & Puri (2021). Approximate finite-energy state representations are discussed by Matsuura, Yamasaki & Koashi (2020).

Metric: squared state fidelity, Jozsa, Fidelity for Mixed Quantum States (1994), reducing to|⟨ψ|χ⟩|² for pure states. Sampler-distribution check: Massart (1990). Bibliographic correction (19 November 2026): the frozen pre-run protocol misattributes PRX Quantum 2, 020101; its authors are Grimsmo and Puri, as cited here. The Gaussian-mixture identity, optimized evaluation, inverse-CDF algorithm and reference weighting are our implementation, independently checked here. This experiment is not a reproduction of a published numerical performance value.

Evidence and limits

Decision summary and numerical checks · Held-out accuracy CSV · Memory metrics CSV · Complete run record · Frozen pre-run protocol

The accuracy comparison covers fixed states and finite operators, not all states or hardware. The eight-cycle study covers one noise setting and the nearest-lattice controller; LSTM and Bayes conclusions do not follow. The thresholds are empirical numerical budgets and refinement checks, not rigorous infinite-cutoff bounds. All source snapshots and raw hashes are verified before rendering. Figures are embedded for offline viewing.
